claim: Only seed 25 completed; the seed 24 run failed. In seed 25, the accel_step probe was decoded well at layer 4 (R2 = 0.832 vs control 0.517, margin 0.314), but its symbolic fit was (a/r - 0.416)*0.0127*a ≈ 0.0127*a^2/r - 0.0053*a. That has an r exponent of -1, not -2, an a exponent of about 2, not 3, and a fit error of 0.254 against the true law. This meets the pre-registered falsification condition (probe R2 >= 0.8 with r exponent in [-1.4, -0.6]) even with m2 fixed and e in [0, 0.7]. By comparison, force had R2 = 0.630 vs control 0.391 (margin 0.239) and fit 0.723/r (error 0.488). Distance had R2 0.866 vs control 0.172 and energy 0.936 vs 0.179, both at layer 1, and val_mse_ratio = 0.014.
confidence_note: This rests on one seed. Seed 24 (run-20261011-223558-e03f) failed with an infrastructure error (FileNotFoundError when renaming the dataset cache file data.tmp.npz to data.npz), not for any scientific reason, so 'supported' was never reachable: it needed both seeds. The refutation clause only needed one seed, but several things limit confidence. Probe R2 of 0.832 is only just above the 0.8 threshold. The fit error of 0.254 falls in the gap between the pass (<0.2) and fail (>=0.3) thresholds. And free-form fits confound a with r because r lies in [a(1-e), a(1+e)], so the a^2/r form could be partly an artifact of the fit. Two results would move this toward inconclusive or supported: a rerun of seed 24 that gives an r exponent in [-2.5, -1.5], or a symbolic fit run on the true accel_step target with the same pipeline and data that also returns r^-1 (which would mean the fitting method, not the model, produces r^-1). Fitting a^p * g(r/a) with p and g fitted separately would also settle the exponent.

claim: With m2 fixed at about 0.5 and e in [0, 0.9], accel_step beats force on headroom-normalized margin in both seeds: 0.40 vs 0.22 for seed 19 (accel_step R2 0.503 at L4 vs control 0.169; force R2 0.351 at L2 vs control 0.163) and 0.34 vs 0.31 for seed 18 (accel_step 0.421 vs 0.125; force 0.433 vs 0.181). But neither accel_step symbolic fit recovers a^3/r^2: seed 19 gives a^2/(r(r+1.66)) with error 0.55, and seed 18 gives a rational function of a and r/a with overall a-degree 1 and error 0.65. The force fits come out as ~1/r again (0.97/r and 1.01/r, errors 0.57 and 0.62), not 1/r^2.
confidence_note: Results are mixed against the pre-registered criteria. The margin prediction holds in both seeds, though narrowly in seed 18 (0.34 vs 0.31; raw margins 0.296 vs 0.252). The fit prediction fails in both seeds: no a exponent lands in [2.5, 3.5] and both errors are above 0.5. Seed 19's a^2 technically meets the expected-if-false condition (a exponent <= 2), but I do not treat that as a refutation, for three reasons. First, the fits are poor (error 0.55-0.65) and come from probe directions with R2 only 0.42-0.50. Second, a and r are strongly correlated because r lies in [a(1-e), a(1+e)], so separate a and r exponents are weakly identifiable. Third, both fitted expressions are roughly homogeneous of degree ~1 in length, which is the same overall scaling as a^3/r^2. The force fits also give r^-1 with m2 fixed, so the r^-1 seen in earlier runs is not an artefact of varying m2. Both runs completed 3000 steps and beat baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.009-0.010). Two things would change the verdict: a fit on a probe with R2 >= 0.8 (MLP or log target) that recovers a^~3 r^~-2 would support the hypothesis, and a fit that keeps r^-1 with an a exponent <= 2 would refute it.

claim: Refuted. With eccentricity widened to [0, 0.9] (and m2 in [0.01, 1]), the symbolic fit to the best accel_step-probe direction still comes out as r^-1 rather than r^-2 in both seeds, even though the accel_step probe beats its random control. Seed 16: 0.0103*a^2/r, fit_error_vs_true_law 0.71, accel_step R2 0.395 vs control 0.175 (margin 0.220). Seed 17: 0.00277*((a+0.685)^3/r - r), which is roughly a^3 but still r^-1, fit_error 0.62, accel_step R2 0.503 vs control 0.182 (margin 0.321). Accel_step beats force in both seeds: force R2 0.154 vs control 0.057 (margin 0.097, fails the 0.1 threshold) and 0.237 vs control 0.131 (margin 0.106). The force fits were m2/r + 0.40 and (m2 + 0.60)/r, errors 0.90 and 0.64. Prediction stays strong: val_mse_ratio 0.0137 and 0.0128.
confidence_note: Both seeds meet the expected-if-false criteria on their own: accel_step margin >= 0.1, r exponent about -1, fit error >= 0.3. Seed 16 also has an a exponent of 2. The main caveat is that the accel_step probe direction explains only 40-50% of accel_step variance at e <= 0.9, down from 0.92-0.95 at e <= 0.5. So the symbolic fit describes a weak linear approximation. The r^-1 result could come from a linear probe failing to follow the heavy-tailed 1/r^2 near pericentre, rather than from the model encoding an r^-1 quantity. Three things would flip this to inconclusive or supported: (1) an MLP probe or a log(accel_step) probe reaches R2 >= 0.8 and its fitted direction gives r^-2; (2) fits restricted to systems in a narrow band of a give r^-2; (3) further seeds recover r^-2. Data seed 0 is shared by both runs, and probing was final-only.

claim: Fixing m2 at 0.5, so that force is exactly 0.5/r^2, did not lift the force probe. Final force R2 was 0.750 at layer 1 (seed 14, control 0.560, margin 0.19) and 0.732 at layer 2 (seed 15, control 0.508, margin 0.224). accel_step reached 0.924 and 0.946 at layer 4 (controls 0.743 and 0.762, margins 0.18), a raw R2 lead of 0.17-0.21 over force. Distance was decoded at 0.87-0.89, so the force ceiling of about 0.73-0.75 comes from the 1/r^2 nonlinearity or how the layers encode it, not from m2 information missing from the residual stream.
confidence_note: Both seeds independently meet every expected-if-false criterion by a wide margin: force R2 is at most 0.78 (0.75 and 0.73, inside the 0.65-0.74 band from spread-m2 runs), and accel_step leads by at least 0.12 (0.175 and 0.215). Neither seed approaches the 0.85 force R2 the hypothesis predicted. The main limit is that both runs stopped before 3000 steps. Seed 14 stopped at step 1500 (val_mse_ratio 0.063) and seed 15 at step 2500 (0.0145). The later, better-trained seed has the slightly lower force R2, so more training is unlikely to close a gap of more than 0.1, but this is not proven. Only linear probes were used. A nonlinear or log-target probe that decodes force at 0.85 or higher with m2 fixed would show the ceiling is a linear-readout artifact rather than a representational one, though it would still not support the m2 hypothesis. A full 3000-step run showing force R2 at 0.85 or above would reopen the question.

history.note: truncated run no longer counts as an agreeing seed

notes.text: Demoted from replicated: seed 14 (run-20261011-213802-00ed) trained only 55% of its planned steps because of a pipeline bug in the budget hard stop, so only seed 15 is valid evidence. A fresh-seed replication has been queued.

claim: The pre-registered refutation condition was met: in seed 12 the fitted accel_step direction scales as a^2/r (r exponent -1), not a^3/r^2. Neither seed met the success criteria, since both fits scale as a^2 rather than a^3 and both fit errors exceed 0.2 (seed 12: 0.202, seed 13: 0.233). Seed 13's fit, a^2*0.0113/(m2*r^2 + r), runs between r^-1 (small m2) and r^-2 (m2 near 1). Both runs finished all 3000 steps (val_mse_ratio 0.015 / 0.017). The accel_step probe clearly beats control (R2 0.917 / 0.883 vs control 0.738 / 0.674, margins 0.179 / 0.210, layer 4). The force probe has the larger margin (R2 0.707 / 0.712 vs control 0.451 / 0.468, margins 0.257 / 0.243, layers 1-2). As the hypothesis predicted, the force-direction fit does not recover m2/r^2: it gives (m2 + 0.24)/r and (m2 + 0.26)/r, with fit errors 0.41 / 0.39.
confidence_note: The verdict rests on the pre-registered clause 'at least one seed keeps an r exponent near -1', which seed 12 meets cleanly. Seed 13 is in between: its r exponent depends on m2 and its fit error of 0.233 is between the true (<0.2) and false (>=0.3) thresholds, so the two seeds do not independently agree. One major caveat: with eccentricity in [0, 0.5], r stays within a factor of about 1.5-3 of a. That makes a^3/r^2, a^2/r and a nearly collinear, so symbolic regression may not be able to tell these forms apart. 'a^2/r instead of a^3/r^2' may therefore reflect an identifiability limit of the data rather than a different learned law. Both probe margins clearly beat control in both seeds, so some gravity-like structure is there; what is in doubt is its exact form. The verdict would weaken toward inconclusive or flip to supported if fits on data where r and a are decorrelated (eccentricity up to 0.9, or per-snapshot fits at fixed a) recovered r^-2 with a^3 in both seeds. It would strengthen if r^-1 persisted under those conditions.

claim: Once training covers e in [0, 0.8], the high-eccentricity gap is gone in both seeds. On held-out high-e systems val_mse_ratio is 0.0187 (seed 9) and 0.0189 (seed 8), about 1.05x and 1.01x the in-distribution 0.0178 and 0.0187, and no worse than held-out low-e (0.0185, 0.0215). The probes still beat their random controls at the last checkpoint: force margin 0.208 (R2 0.452 vs control 0.244, layer 4) and 0.312 (0.528 vs 0.216, layer 1); accel_step margin 0.337 (0.715 vs 0.378) and 0.358 (0.707 vs 0.349), both at layer 4. accel_step has the larger margin over its control than force in both seeds.
confidence_note: Both seeds clearly meet the expected-if-true criteria: the high-e/in-distribution ratio is about 1.0x against a 3x threshold, and every probe margin is at least 0.2 against a 0.1 threshold. Three things limit confidence. (1) Both runs stopped at step 2500 of 3000 after using only 0.13 of the 0.2 h budget, and val_mse_ratio was still falling (0.034 to 0.018 over the last 500 steps). The 'final' checkpoint is therefore step 2500 and the models had not converged. Stopping early should not reverse a 1x vs 3x result, but it is unexplained. (2) This shows the earlier 16-18x gap was a coverage gap in prediction. It does not show the internal representation works equally well at high e: the best force probe R2 on held-out high-e is only 0.366-0.377, against 0.729-0.802 on held-out low-e, while prediction error is the same on both. That repeats the earlier drop to 0.34-0.40, and there is no random control on the eval sets, so this probe drop is not explained. (3) Two seeds, one data seed, one architecture (L=4, d=64, N=64). The verdict would weaken if training to 3000 steps or a further seed opened a high-e gap above 3x, or if an OOD random control showed the force probe does not beat chance on high-e systems.

claim: With m2 spread over [0.01, 1], accel_step beat its control in both seeds: R2 0.915 vs control 0.712 (margin 0.203, seed 11) and 0.924 vs 0.760 (margin 0.164, seed 10), both at layer 4. Force did slightly better on raw margin at layer 1 (0.735 vs 0.519, margin 0.216; 0.648 vs 0.452, margin 0.196), but accel_step led on headroom-normalized margin (0.70 vs 0.45 and 0.68 vs 0.36). The symbolic fits only partly matched the prediction. The force direction fit to (m2 + c)/r in both seeds: it has a positive m2 factor but an r exponent of -1, not -2. The accel_step direction fit to roughly a^3/(r*(r + m2^3)) in seed 10 (close to a^3/r^2 with no positive m2 factor; error vs true law 0.128) but to about a^2/r in seed 11 (error 0.308). Neither run recovered the law.
confidence_note: Both seeds met the margin and headroom-normalized-margin parts of expected_if_true. However, both runs stopped at step 2000 of the 3000 configured, so the 'final checkpoint' is early, and the symbolic part is mixed. Only seed 10's accel_step fit has an r exponent near -2 with orbit-scale (a^3) dependence. Seed 11's fit is roughly r^-1, and both force fits are r^-1, so they match neither the force law nor the accel_step law. Neither fit counts as recovered (fit errors 0.13-0.41). The m2 factor in the force fit may just reflect the force target, which contains m2, rather than show that the model encodes m2. accel_step's control R2 is high (0.71-0.76), which caps its raw margin. This would become supported if full-length 3000-step runs gave accel_step fits with r^-2 and a^3 dependence and no positive m2 term in both seeds. It would become refuted if a fit recovered m2/r^2 for the gravity direction, or if force's normalized margin caught up with accel_step's.

claim: The predictor transferred to low mass ratios but not, by the pre-registered 10x criterion, to high eccentricities. In-distribution val_mse_ratio was 0.0151 (seed 7) and 0.0157 (seed 6). On low_mass_ratio (m2 in [0.01, 0.1]) it was 0.057 and 0.055, about 3.6x in-distribution, and the best force R2 held at 0.75-0.77. On high_eccentricity (e in [0.5, 0.8]) it was 0.270 and 0.249, about 16-18x in-distribution, and the best force R2 fell to 0.40 and 0.34, down from 0.74 and 0.69 in-distribution. Every two-body ratio stayed below 1. At the final checkpoint, in-distribution probes beat their random controls in both seeds: force 0.738 vs 0.529 and 0.689 vs 0.523 (margins 0.209 and 0.166, best at layer 1), and accel_step 0.934 vs 0.757 and 0.935 vs 0.727 (margins 0.178 and 0.208, best at layer 4). Three-body ratios of 72 and 70 are exploratory only.
confidence_note: The refutation rests on one pre-registered clause: high_eccentricity ratios are more than 10x the in-distribution ratio while in-distribution stays below 0.05. Both seeds meet it by a clear margin (15.8x and 17.9x). The failure is partial, though. The model still beats constant-velocity extrapolation about 4x on high-e systems, and mass-ratio transfer passed every criterion, so the result is 'depends on the training range of e', not 'no law-like structure'. The 10x threshold is arbitrary, and constant-velocity extrapolation may itself do much worse at high e, so the ratio is not directly comparable across sets. OOD probe R2 values come without random controls, so the drop in force R2 on high-e systems cannot be read as a margin. The verdict would move toward inconclusive if (a) the absolute MSE gap mostly comes from a few pericentre snapshots where r falls below the training range, which would be smooth extrapolation error rather than a shortcut, or (b) a model trained on e in [0, 0.8] showed the same degradation on held-out high-e systems.

claim: In both seeds, the accel_step margin first reaches ≥ 0.1 at step 100 (layer 4; 0.115 for seed 4, 0.108 for seed 5). At step 100, val_mse_ratio is still 1.96 and 1.84, and it is first reported below 1 at step 175 (0.736 and 0.878), so accel_step structure appears at least one 25-step checkpoint before the model beats constant-velocity extrapolation. Distance (margin 0.65 and 0.63 by step 50, formed_at_step 25) and energy (formed_at_step 25) form even earlier, while val_mse_ratio is still 5 to 83. Force forms later or not at all: final margins are 0.068 (seed 4, never ≥ 0.1) and 0.103 (seed 5, formed_at_step 450), against accel_step final margins of 0.156 and 0.165.
confidence_note: Both seeds agree exactly on the step where accel_step forms (100) and on the order: distance and energy, then accel_step, then val_mse_ratio < 1, then force (late or never). The trajectories reported here skip steps 125 and 150, so the first checkpoint below 1 is somewhere between 125 and 175. That does not affect the verdict, because at step 100 val_mse_ratio is still > 1.8 in both seeds. The main weakness is that the accel_step margins at the crossing (0.108, 0.115) are only just above the 0.1 threshold. If the threshold were 0.12, the crossing would move to about step 175 and coincide with val < 1 rather than come before it. Distance and energy crossing at step 25, while the model is far worse than baseline, suggests early probe-readable geometry that does not yet help prediction, possibly reshaping of the input embedding rather than computation tied to gravity. Seed 5's val_mse_ratio goes back above 1 at step 225 (1.057), so 'first beats baseline' is not a stable transition. The verdict would change if denser checkpoints (every 5-10 steps), a stricter margin, or more seeds showed the accel_step crossing landing at or after the val < 1 point, or if accel_step-specific margin vanished once distance is regressed out. The force margin here (0.07-0.10) is much smaller than in earlier runs (0.22-0.24), which also used different configs, so the force results do not carry over directly.

claim: Refuted. Widening m2 to [0.01, 1] did not make the force probe fall behind accel_step. In both seeds the force margin over control was larger than the accel_step margin at the final checkpoint: seed 2 force R2 0.737 vs control 0.494 (margin 0.243, layer 4) against accel_step R2 0.914 vs control 0.709 (margin 0.205, layer 4); seed 3 force R2 0.681 vs control 0.446 (margin 0.235, layer 1) against accel_step R2 0.928 vs control 0.753 (margin 0.175, layer 4). accel_step still led on raw R2 by 0.18-0.25 and kept its margin above 0.1, so the probe was not broken. The force margins were also not >= 0.05 below the default-mass-range E5 margins (0.223-0.230); they were about the same or slightly higher. Both models beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.0114 and 0.0119).
confidence_note: The pre-registered margin criterion is met in both seeds, but it is biased against accel_step. accel_step's random control is already 0.71-0.75, so its margin cannot exceed about 0.25-0.29, while force has about 0.51-0.55 of headroom. Measured as a fraction of headroom, (R2-control)/(1-control), accel_step leads: 0.70 vs 0.48 in seed 2 and 0.71 vs 0.42 in seed 3. So this result says the model keeps force-specific signal beyond the control; it does not show that force is the primary representation. Force and accel_step remain collinear through 1/r^2, and force's best layer differs between seeds (1 vs 4), so the force signal may partly be distance or 1/r^2 (distance margin is 0.64-0.70). The E5 comparison uses margins reported in an earlier question, not a run checked here for exactly matched settings. The verdict would change if a probe on force with accel_step and distance regressed out kept no margin over control, or if a headroom-normalized criterion were adopted.

claim: In both seeds, gravity-related probes beat their controls at the first trained checkpoint (step 250). The accel_step margin was 0.158 (seed 2) and 0.127 (seed 3) at layer 4, and the distance margin was 0.597 and 0.681 at layer 1. That is 1250 steps before val_mse_ratio first fell below 0.1, which happened at step 1500 in both seeds (0.0858 and 0.0985). Final val_mse_ratio was about 0.011. Force formed no earlier than accel_step: margin 0.107 at step 250 in seed 2 and 0.127 at step 750 in seed 3. By step 4000 the force margin (0.223, 0.230) had overtaken the accel_step margin (0.204, 0.172), even though accel_step had the higher raw R2 (0.914 and 0.925 vs control 0.710 and 0.752, compared with force 0.738 and 0.696 vs control 0.516 and 0.465).
confidence_note: Both seeds agree on the ordering, and the gap is large: 5 checkpoints, against the 1-checkpoint tolerance. Five things limit confidence. (1) The first-checkpoint accel_step margins are only just over the threshold (0.127 and 0.158 against 0.1), and accel_step's random-control R2 is high (0.71-0.75), so a small change in the control could move the formation step. (2) Structure is already present at step 250, when val_mse_ratio is still 0.87. The 250-step checkpoint spacing cannot say whether it forms before or together with the first drop below the baseline. (3) The trajectories have no entries at steps 500, 1250, 2000, 2750 or 3500, so the logs are incomplete. (4) The large early distance margin may partly reflect geometry that is easy to read from the input, not learned dynamics. (5) Forming early shows only correlation in time; it does not show the model uses this structure to predict. The verdict would change if denser early checkpoints (every 25 steps) showed accel_step margins crossing 0.1 only after val_mse_ratio had already fallen far below 1, or if seeds 4 and 5, or a different width, showed accel_step forming after step 1500.

claim: This is one cell of the scaling grid (L=2, d_model=32, n_systems=1000, seed 0), so it cannot test whether force R2 rises monotonically with model and data size. At the final step (val_mse_ratio = 0.076), the force probe has R2 = 0.692 at layer 1 vs control 0.394 (margin 0.298), and the accel_step probe has R2 = 0.788 at layer 2 vs control 0.584 (margin 0.204). Distance has R2 = 0.838 vs control 0.014 (margin 0.824).
confidence_note: This experiment alone cannot settle the hypothesis. A monotonic trend needs the other grid cells (other L, d_model and n_systems values) compared on the same margin metric, and that comparison is not available here. The result is one seed with final-checkpoint probes only, so formed_at_step = 3000 is just the only step that was probed, not when the structure appeared. In this cell, force (margin 0.298) beats its control by more than accel_step does (margin 0.204). That is the reverse of the earlier finding, where accel_step had the higher raw R2 (0.917 vs force's 0.728). It does not show a physical-force representation: accel_step's raw R2 is still higher (0.788 vs 0.692), its control is unusually high (0.584), and the two targets are collinear through 1/r^2. The verdict would become supported or refuted once the full grid is compared on force margin, ideally with 2 or more seeds per cell. The force-vs-accel_step reading would change if the force margin collapses after accel_step is regressed out.

claim: The 4-layer transformer (seed 1) clearly beats constant-velocity extrapolation on held-out systems: final val_mse_ratio = 0.0051 (MSE 1.31e-7 vs baseline 2.55e-5). The ratio fell below 1 by step 500 (0.774) and below 0.1 by step 1250 (0.084). At the final checkpoint, the accel_step probe (R2 = 0.917 at layer 1, control 0.742, margin 0.175) is stronger in absolute terms than the force probe (R2 = 0.729 at layer 4, control 0.507, margin 0.222). Distance (0.973 vs 0.769) and energy (0.832 vs 0.660) also beat their controls. Velocity does not (0.955 vs 0.878, margin 0.078 < 0.1).
confidence_note: The verdict covers only the stated hypothesis (val_mse_ratio < 1). The ratio of 0.005 sits about 200x below the threshold, so the result is not borderline, but it comes from one seed and one data seed. A second seed with val_mse_ratio >= 1 would be needed to overturn it, which is unlikely given the size of the gap. The probe results add context but are weak evidence on their own. The random-model controls are high (0.51-0.88), so much of each target is linearly readable from the input encoding. Force and accel_step both scale as 1/r^2 and are correlated across this dataset, so this run cannot say which one the model encodes. Force has the larger margin over control but the lower R2, and it peaks at a different layer (4 vs 1). Probes were run only at the final checkpoint, so formed_at_step = 5000 means 'present at the last checkpoint', not 'formed at step 5000'.

claim: The 4-layer transformer beat constant-velocity extrapolation on held-out two-body systems by about 200x: val_mse_ratio = 0.0051 (MSE 1.31e-7 vs baseline 2.55e-5), and the ratio stayed below 1 from step 500 onward (0.354 at step 500). Secondary probe readout at the final checkpoint: force R2 = 0.728 at layer 2 vs control 0.526 (margin 0.20), distance R2 = 0.967 vs 0.655, energy R2 = 0.791 vs 0.538, and velocity R2 = 0.952 vs control 0.888, which falls short of the 0.1 margin; accel_step was not probed, so we can't tell whether the force signal reflects physical force or the per-snapshot version.
confidence_note: Only one seed (seed 0) on one dataset (data_seed 0), so this is weak evidence, although the effect is large: the ratio is about 200x below the threshold of 1. With N = 64 snapshots per orbit and e <= 0.5, the constant-velocity baseline is weak, so beating it shows good next-step prediction, not that the model learned the physical law. The validation curve was not monotonic (0.098 at step 1000, 0.142 at step 1250; 0.043 at 2250, 0.053 at 2750), but it never came near 1. Probes were run only at the final checkpoint, so formed_at_step = 5000 says nothing about when the structure formed. The verdict would change if replication with other seeds or data seeds gave val_mse_ratio >= 1, or if the result failed to hold on out-of-distribution eval sets (higher eccentricity, different mass ratios).
